superseded_in_part: 2026-09-26: the '13 coordinates, one positive' scope here is stale. Five of the thirteen now answer structurally, B01/B03 answer through the approved successor income input, and the predecessor FY2024 amendment is now classified (historical_amendment_note), so there are two positives. The current scope is statement-values-request.json: 8 coordinates at 2024-12-31 and 6 at 2025-12-31. The recommendation is per-amendment, evidence-constrained admission, not a two-condition rule for future Part III amendments.

the_decision_this_needs.not_taken_unilaterally: no policy file or clearing rule was changed by this review.

recommended_option.cost: a revision to config/annual_amendment_scope_v1.json and the two-line clearing rule in annual_amendment_scope.py, through the existing revision mechanism, with the historical semantics preserved.
recommended_option.effect_if_taken: 13 coordinates on this period stop being refused. It does not make them correct - they would then have to run, and content acceptance is separate as everywhere else.
recommended_option.what: let a Part III addition clear ORIGINAL_STATEMENT_VALUES only when both mechanical proofs hold: the no-financial-statement declaration is present, and the amendment carries no native fact outside the governance taxonomy.
recommended_option.why: it keeps the standing rule intact - nothing clears automatically, the classification alone still clears nothing - while letting a case that proves itself through. A Part III amendment that did restate something would carry a financial fact and would still be refused.

the_alternative.what: keep the refusal and keep the 13 in the denominator with this finding attached
the_alternative.why_someone_might_prefer_it: a conditional rule is still a rule written from one amendment. Only one Part III amendment exists in this repository's saved material, so the condition has been tested on a single positive and no negative.

the_decision_this_needs.who: the owner, because it changes which inputs a metric will accept, which is a correctness standard rather than an implementation choice. The repository's standing rule is that Part III does not AUTOMATICALLY approve a financial or subject-consolidation scope - the word is 'automatically', and this is the non-automatic path.

and.quote: Except as explicitly set forth herein, this Amendment does not otherwise change, modify or update the disclosures in, or exhibits to, the Initial Form 10-K.

three_independent_grounds.quote: ...to amend Part III, Items 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 of the Initial Form 10-K to include the information required by such Items.

three_independent_grounds.ground: an explicit declaration inside the amendment
three_independent_grounds.note: the policy already recognises this sentence - it is no_financial_statement_pattern - and it is what names the classification.
three_independent_grounds.quote: No financial statements or supplemental data are filed with this Amendment. See Index to Financial Statements and Supplemental Data of the Initial Form 10-K.

three_independent_grounds.ground: what the amendment actually carries, counted rather than argued
three_independent_grounds.note: the scope inspector proves the seven are governance taxonomy. No financial-statement fact is filed with the amendment at all, so there is nothing in it a statement-class metric could read even if it tried.

what_this_answers: The approved policy classifies Paramount's amendment as PART_III_ADDITION_WITH_EXPLICIT_NO_NEW_FINANCIAL_STATEMENTS, clears the event window, does not clear ORIGINAL_STATEMENT_VALUES, and sets original_statement_admission_requires_further_review. That flag is the policy asking for a review; this is the review. It is not the decision.

what_this_finding_does_not_cover.other_part_iii_amendments: this is about this amendment. Another Part III amendment could restate something, and the policy's caution as a class is not wrong in general.
what_this_finding_does_not_cover.subject_continuity: unrelated and still separately required. Paramount's successor/predecessor question is not answered here.
what_this_finding_does_not_cover.the_nine_not_covered_metric_ids: B06, B13, C02, C03, C04, D01, D02, D03, D04 stay refused whatever the classification, and that is right: Item 13 related-party and Item 10 governance content is exactly what several of them read. This finding does not touch them.

why_it_matters: 13 coordinates - A05, A06, A07, A08, A10, B01, B02, B03, B04, B05, B07, B08, B09 - are refused on this period. 'Needs further review' is not 'permanently unsupported', so they stay in the denominator.
